correctness.rationale: Richomme--Saari--Zamboni prove the Tribonacci word is 2-balanced. Hence every equal-length Parikh difference has coordinate sum zero and coordinates in [-2,2]. The complete nonzero integer list has only equality directions, represented by (1,-1,0), and midpoint directions, represented by (2,-1,-1). Distinct non-arithmetic-progression weights annihilate none of these directions, proving sufficiency. Repeated weights collide already at length 1. The three possible midpoint relations are each realized by explicit Tribonacci factor pairs, proving necessity. The packaged verifier checks the witnesses, all 18 difference directions, and extensive direct finite data.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly asks when valuations make additive and abelian complexities coincide and gives only sufficient constructions, with {0,1,3} as a Tribonacci example. The result replaces that one-sided existence statement by a complete parameter-space classification for an archetypal 2-balanced word: exactly six linear obstruction hyperplanes. This is a natural structural sharpening, not an arbitrary finite parameter check.
